title: Threat model document published for the jury
outcome: One-page threat model the jury reads before D11 live attacks: assets, trust boundaries, in/out of scope, claims we make and refuse
acceptance: Lists assets (state, outbox, record+witness heads, 4 key classes, containment state, PII side store) and the 4 trust boundaries

In scope: buggy, rogue (arbitrary Python in its subprocess), colluding (root candidates only), insider log tamper without keys; out of scope listed with production mitigation (HSM, WORM, uid/container)
Claims match CALL-01 wording exactly: 'tamper-evident up to the last witnessed head'; key isolation 'enforced in production, detected here by reconciliation'; no prevention claim for collusion
Maps every in-scope adversary to the RT# attacks that exercise it and the control that answers it (D6/D7/D8, rules 1-11)
Fits on 2 pages, no unmeasured numbers (D13); panel signs off
summary:
v3 of org/adr/THREAT-MODEL.md applies the panel's must-fix, the length trims and the nit.
(1) Sibling hijack: the Live setup now gives each agent its own numeric uid (60001 + index, no passwd entry needed), and the agent template sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 before agent code runs. rlimits are per uid. I checked this in the container on 19 Nov (/tmp/kabir_uidtest/uidtest.py). subprocess user=int and preexec setuid both give children distinct uids. Cross-uid ptrace and pidfd_getfd return EPERM, whether the victim is dumpable or not. Under one shared uid, both calls succeed on a dumpable sibling, which confirms the finding. They return EPERM again once the sibling is non-dumpable.
(2) New §5 row. Rogue | RT3b | ptrace/pidfd_getfd on a sibling to use its socket and signer handle | per-agent uid + non-dumpable agents; rule 2 | attach gets EPERM; 0 actions attributed to the victim.
(3) The Live setup states that if per-agent uids fail, per-agent attribution is void for that run. The out-of-scope shared-uid row is updated to match.
(4) RT3b is added to tests/redteam/SPEC.md: a catalogue row and a short section with the precondition, NOT_ENFORCEABLE fallback, script outline and boolean pass.
Length: dropped the 'Detect, not exclude' paragraph and folded 'no printed head = out of scope (WORM)' into the record+heads row. Moved the Changes note out of the jury copy into org/adr/THREAT-MODEL-CHANGES.md. §6 is kept.
Nit: the insider now 'edits record files; holds no witness key; cannot alter the head printed at run end (the head store is defence in depth)'.
review:
[panel · changes] CHANGES (4 must-fix, 1 should-fix; this still fits on 2 pages). Assets, B1-B4, in/out of scope with HSM/WORM/uid mitigations, the RT1-RT12 mapping (all 12 present, every in-scope adversary covered) and D13 target labelling all pass. C1-C5 are CALL-01 wording verbatim.
(1) C6 misplaces CALL-01 wording. 'We hold, never cancel' is CALL-01's release semantics for containment, not a recovery claim. As written, C6 says recovery never cancels, which contradicts the C5 RecoveryPlan step cancel_outbox and the demo, where the held payment is discarded in recovery. A jury watching the demo will catch it. Reword C6: 'Containment holds, never cancels (release = un-hold + restore epoch). Recovery appends compensating records; a held outbox item is cancelled only by an approved recovery-plan step (cancel_outbox) after the dry-run diff.'
(2) The key-read gap is acceptable only if its consequence is stated. Under the shared-uid fallback, the jury's sanctioned live attack (arbitrary Python in the rogue subprocess, D11) can read gateway and witness keys. That is the out-of-scope 'both keys' case, so C1 and C4 fail and reconciliation does not see it. §7 currently draws the line at 'a host shell as the gateway's user', which is not the same thing. Add: which setup runs live (separate uid or not, fixed by day 1), and if the uid is shared, that a key read from the rogue subprocess is the admitted gap and voids C1/C4 for that run. RT2 stays the test.
(3) Where do witness heads live? An insider who truncates or rolls back BOTH the record and the witness heads to an older valid prefix passes verify: the 'last witnessed head' just moves back. This is the truncation hole from PANEL-ENG-00 item 2. Fix: state that witness heads are stored by the witness process outside the insider's write access, and add a row for record + witness truncation or rollback. Either detect it (witness keeps its own monotonic store) or put it out of scope (production: WORM witness log).
(4) Availability is not admitted. A rogue that sleeps or loops forever stalls the tick barrier, so every independent agent stops: the 'kill everything' outcome F6 claims to avoid. A fork or memory bomb is the same class. A hostile jury tries this first. Add a rogue row: per-tick deadline, a missing envelope counts as a no-op plus an anomaly. Or state availability and resource exhaustion as out of scope (production: container limits).
(5) Should-fix: the recovery key and Control actions have no row. Assets list 'forge a repair', but nothing says who signs suspend, release, revoke or recover, or that the recovery key never enters an agent process. Add one line: gateway-held, used only on console approval of the dry-run diff, rules 2 and 10; the console operator is trusted.
Gaps: splitting under thresholds with no RT and no claim is ACCEPTABLE as stated (GUARDRAILS X30 backs it). Key reads: acceptable once (2) is done.
Nits: TERMS bans 'quarantine' (RT5, use 'suspension') and 'log' (rule 9, use 'record'). Map the PII side store asset to the F3 pytest.

[panel · changes] CHANGES: 1 must-fix, which is new and caused by v2's Live setup; the rest passes. All 5 earlier fixes are applied correctly. (1) C6 is my wording verbatim and agrees with GUARDRAILS F11/X29/§3. (2) The Live setup is fixed for day 1, and the shared-uid consequence (key read from the rogue voids C1/C4 for that run; RT2 stays the test) is stated and repeated in the out-of-scope table. (3) The witness head store, the monotonic count and the record+heads truncation row are present, with the printed head as the anchor and WORM for runs without one. (4) The stall/fork/memory-bomb row is present: per-tick deadline, missing envelope = no-op + anomaly, rlimits, container limits out of scope. (5) The Control-action/recovery-key row is present and the operator is trusted. Nits fixed: no 'quarantine'/'log' left, side store mapped to F3.\nMUST-FIX: sibling-agent hijack (framing with a valid signature). The Live setup puts ALL agents on 'a separate unprivileged uid', one uid shared by every agent, and the out-of-scope table lists 'separate uid/container per agent' as production-only. Under the sanctioned D11 attack (arbitrary Python in the rogue), a same-uid process can ptrace an honest sibling, or use pidfd_getfd / process_vm_readv on it, and take its gateway socket and signer handle. This sandbox has no Yama (/proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope is absent), so the classic same-uid ptrace rule applies. The rogue then submits envelopes signed by crm's key through crm's handle. By C4's own wording that is a valid signature attributing the action to crm, so D7 anti-framing, F4 identity and RT11 are defeated without a key read, and no RT exercises this. A hostile jury will try it once they see one shared agent uid. Fix: (a) Live setup: 'agents: one unprivileged uid per agent (numeric, e.g. 20000+index; root can setuid to any uid without a passwd entry), and the agent template sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 before agent code runs'. Per-agent uids also make RLIMIT_NPROC per-agent, which helps the fork-bomb row. (b) Add a §5 row: Rogue | RT3 (variant) | ptrace/pidfd_getfd on a sibling agent to use its socket and signer handle | per-agent uid + non-dumpable agent processes; rule 2 | 0 envelopes accepted through another agent's handle. (c) If per-agent uids fail in an environment, say so in the Live setup sentence beside the C1/C4 one: attribution to a specific honest agent is void for that run. Kabir/Maya: add sibling-hijack to the RT2/RT3 test.\nLENGTH (~1,630 words, criterion '2 pages'): ACCEPTABLE. It is table-dense, every row answers a jury attack, and the jury reads it before the live break, where completeness matters more than brevity. Before publishing, keep it to 2 rendered pages: (i) drop the 'Changes v2 (panel)' line from the jury copy (it is internal process; the issue log keeps it); (ii) drop the 'Detect, not exclude' paragraph, because the record+heads row already says it (fold 'a run with no printed head is out of scope (WORM)' into that row's control cell). That saves ~90 words. Do not cut §6: §5 cites the rules by number.\nNit: the insider definition says 'no write access to the witness head store', but the record is gateway-owned (uid 0, 0600), so anyone able to edit it is effectively root and can also write the 0700 store. The printed head is the real anchor and the store is defence in depth. Word the insider as 'edits record files; holds no witness key; cannot alter the head printed at run end'. Re-review is quick: one row and two Live-setup clauses.

[panel · done] DONE. Signed off for the jury. v3 fixes the sibling-hijack must-fix, applies the trims and fixes the nit.
(1) PER-AGENT UID + NON-DUMPABLE: PASS, independently re-run. I ran /tmp/kabir_uidtest/uidtest.py with python3 -I from /tmp as uid 0, today. subprocess user=60001/60002 gives those uids with no passwd entry, and preexec setuid gives 60003. With the attacker as uid 60002 and the victim as uid 60001, ptrace and pidfd_getfd both return EPERM, whether the victim is dumpable or not. With the same uid and a dumpable victim, both succeed (ptrace OK, pidfd_getfd fd 4), which confirms the original finding. With the same uid and a non-dumpable victim, both return EPERM. Yama is absent. process_vm_readv and /proc/pid/mem go through the same ptrace-attach check, and RT3b also probes vm_read. The Live setup states it correctly: numeric uid 60001 + index, PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 set in the template before agent code (after exec, which is right), per-uid rlimits (helps the fork-bomb row). Per-agent uids also stop cross-agent kill(), a small availability bonus.
(2) RT3b ROW: PASS. The §5 row has the attack, the control (per-agent uid + non-dumpable; rule 2) and a boolean target. §7 now lists 'attaching to sibling agents' as sanctioned. SPEC.md has the catalogue row and a section with the precondition, the NOT_ENFORCEABLE fallback, ptrace/getfd/vm_read probes, a pass check that compares attribution to the oracle, and a documented control run that is not asserted.
(3) VOID-ATTRIBUTION FALLBACK: PASS. The Live setup sentence sits beside the C1/C4 one. The out-of-scope shared-uid row covers both cases (agent = gateway user voids C1/C4; agents sharing a uid void per-agent attribution). C4's refuse cell ('which key signed through which handle') agrees.
(4) TRIMS: PASS. The 'Detect, not exclude' paragraph is dropped. The WORM no-printed-head clause is folded into the truncation row. The Changes note moved to THREAT-MODEL-CHANGES.md. §6 is kept. Length is about 1,630 words against about 1,600 in v2, and the table density is the same, so it is still 2 rendered pages.
(5) INSIDER WORDING: PASS, verbatim as requested.
No 'quarantine' or 'log' in the jury copy. Targets are labelled D13. C1-C6 are unchanged.
Nits (no re-review): (a) §5 RT3b target, '0 actions attributed to the victim', reads literally as crm doing nothing. Make it '0 rogue actions attributed to the victim', matching SPEC's 'beyond its own'. (b) SPEC.md line 77, RT5 'TOCTOU at quarantine': TERMS bans the word, use 'suspension'. This is in SPEC, not the jury copy. (c) 'Checked here 19 Nov' is a measured fact, not a target, so D13 is fine. Keep the script in the repo (tests/redteam) so the claim is reproducible, not only in /tmp.
